title: High-Level Contextual Vocabulary
tagline: Year 4 — Less common words (ephemeral, ostensible, perfunctory) understood from sentence clues and word parts

introduction.overview: Advanced vocabulary questions use less common words in sentences that give enough clues to decide the meaning. The clues are contrast, restatement, example, cause and tone, and the word parts (prefixes and roots) often confirm the guess. This chapter practises 20 such words and the method of reading the sentence first and the options second.
introduction.placementRelevance: Higher-level vocabulary appears in reading comprehension and in direct word-meaning questions of company and bank tests.
introduction.realWorldContext: Professional reading includes unfamiliar words; context lets you follow without a dictionary.

learningObjectives: Use contrast, restatement and example clues
Use tone to rule out opposite meanings
Use roots and prefixes as confirmation
Handle words with positive or negative flavour

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Replace the word with each option; the right one keeps the sentence sensible and the tone consistent.

coreDefinitions: Restatement clue: the sentence explains the word.
Contrast clue: but, however, unlike signal the opposite.
Tone: approval or disapproval carried by the sentence.
Root: a word part with a stable meaning.
Substitution test: putting an option in place of the word.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: The sentence is the dictionary; the options are only a menu.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Cover the word, guess a simple substitute, then find it among the options.

mainNarrative: "The ephemeral beauty of the cherry blossom lasts only a few days." The sentence restates the word: ephemeral means short-lived.
"Despite the setbacks, she remained sanguine" contrasts with setbacks, so sanguine is positive: optimistic.
"His obsequious manner… he praised the manager at every turn" gives the example: excessively eager to please.
"The ostensible reason for the visit was a courtesy call, but he wanted to negotiate": the "but" shows that the stated reason is not the real one, so ostensible means apparent.
"A cursory inspection missed the crack" suggests a hasty, not thorough, inspection.

deepDiveAspects.title: Positive versus negative
deepDiveAspects.content: If the sentence praises, avoid negative options; the tone limits the choice.

deepDiveAspects.title: Roots
deepDiveAspects.content: Equivocate: equi (equal) + voc (voice): to speak with two voices.

solvedExamples.title: Restatement
solvedExamples.question: The ephemeral beauty of the blossom lasts only a few days. What does "ephemeral" mean?

solvedExamples.title: Contrast
solvedExamples.question: Despite the setbacks, she remained sanguine. What does "sanguine" mean?

solvedExamples.title: Example
solvedExamples.question: His obsequious manner made colleagues uneasy; he praised the manager at every turn. What does it mean?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Read the sentence for restatement, contrast or example, guess a substitute, then match it.

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: Drop options with the wrong tone.
placementTips.recruiterInsight: You can often answer without knowing the word.

easy.question:
The ephemeral beauty of the cherry blossom lasts only a few days.

In this sentence, "ephemeral" is closest in meaning to
easy.explanation: The sentence restates the meaning: it lasts only a few days.

easy.question:
Smartphones have become ubiquitous in the city; almost everyone carries one.

In this sentence, "ubiquitous" is closest in meaning to
easy.explanation: The restatement "almost everyone carries one" shows the meaning.

easy.question:
Despite the setbacks, she remained sanguine about the outcome.

In this sentence, "sanguine" is closest in meaning to
easy.explanation: The word contrasts with setbacks, so it is positive.

intermediate.question:
The ostensible reason for the visit was a courtesy call, but he wanted to negotiate.

In this sentence, "ostensible" is closest in meaning to
intermediate.explanation: "But" shows the stated reason was not the real one.

intermediate.question:
The recalcitrant mule refused to move however hard the farmer pulled.

In this sentence, "recalcitrant" is closest in meaning to
intermediate.explanation: Refusing to move despite pulling shows stubborn resistance.

intermediate.question:
Asked whether he agreed, he gave a laconic reply: "Yes."

In this sentence, "laconic" is closest in meaning to
intermediate.explanation: The reply was a single word.

advanced.question:
The villagers venerate the old teacher and visit her every festival.

In this sentence, "venerate" is closest in meaning to
advanced.explanation: Visiting her every festival shows deep respect.

advanced.question:
Her expression was inscrutable; no one could tell what she thought.

In this sentence, "inscrutable" is closest in meaning to
advanced.explanation: The restatement says no one could tell her thoughts.

placementStyle.question:
A cursory inspection of the bridge missed the crack that later grew.

In this sentence, "cursory" is closest in meaning to
placementStyle.explanation: A hasty inspection missed the crack.

placementStyle.question:
His impetuous decision to resign surprised everyone, for he had not discussed it with anyone.

In this sentence, "impetuous" is closest in meaning to

The mercurial star was charming one day and sullen the next.

In this sentence, "mercurial" is closest in meaning to
placementStyle.explanation: The two contrasting days show changeable moods.
